Title: ESpeakTextAudioConverter (Cyrena.Voice.Extension)
Content:
eSpeak TTS converter, mirrors the WebView converter's contract exactly.
- Key: `ESpeakTextAudioConverter.Key` = `"espeak.tts"` (AddKeyedScoped ITextAudioConverter, registered in VoiceExtension.BuildExtension alongside the existing "webview.tts" WebViewTextAudioConverter)
- Config: `ESpeakOptions` (Cyrena.Voice.Options) — BinaryPath, Voice, Speed, Pitch, Amplitude, WordGap. Read per call via ISettingsService, falls back to defaults.
- Mechanism: spawns `espeak "text"` with the configured voice/pace/pitch/volume flags; eSpeak plays directly to the host's default audio device (ALSA/PulseAudio/PipeWire on Linux, default endpoint on Windows). **No IAudioPlayer is required** — eSpeak's own playback handles the audio path. The same fire-and-forget shape as WebViewTextAudioConverter, which lets the browser play via `speechSynthesis`.
- Output: returns an empty `WebViewAudioArtifact` as a marker (same artifact type as the WebView converter, not a new type).
- **Process serialisation (critical)**: instance-level `SemaphoreSlim(1,1)` gates every `ConvertAsync` call. Without it, the streaming sentence queue in `Toolbar.RunQueue` would spawn a fresh eSpeak process per dequeued sentence, and the new process's first ~50–150ms of audio gets dropped/clipped because the previous process hasn't yet released the host audio device (PulseAudio/PipeWire on Linux, WASAPI on Windows). The user heard this as "one or two words, then it cuts off, then the next phrase tries to speak, then cuts off again". Holding the gate across `WaitForExitAsync` ensures the next call doesn't start until the current utterance has fully exited and released the audio device.
- Cancellation: CancellationToken kills the eSpeak process tree and throws OperationCanceledException. The gate is released in `finally` so a cancel does not deadlock the queue.
- Errors: throws InvalidOperationException with stderr context on non-zero exit / missing binary.
- DI scope caveat: the converter is registered **scoped**, so the gate only serialises calls within the same scope. In practice the Toolbar resolves it once for `RunQueue` and never shares with concurrent scopes, so this is correct. If a future call site needs cross-scope serialisation, the gate would need to lift to a singleton or to `Cyrena.Voice.Core`.
- Rejected earlier design (do not resurrect): the "capture WAV to stdout with -w -" approach was tried and discarded. eSpeak plays the speech itself, so the extra code to parse RIFF/WAVE, dodge the 4KB process output buffer, validate the header, and return a new `ESpeakAudioArtifact` was needless complexity. There is no `IAudioPlayer` for it to feed into; the WebView model is correct.
- Final, no leftover `ESpeakAudioArtifact` model class — the only audio model in the namespace is `WebViewAudioArtifact`.
